title.zh: 卷275 列傳六十二 格尔古德 赵士麟 郭世隆 傅臘塔 马如龙
title.en: Volume 275 Biographies 62: Ge Er Gu De, Zhao Shilin, Guo Shilong, Fu Lata, Ma Rulong
title.raw: 卷275 列傳六十二 格尔古德 赵士麟 郭世隆 傅臘塔 马如龙

sentences.zh: 列傳六十二

translations.literal: Biographies 62
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 62

sentences.zh: 格爾古德金世德趙士麟郭世隆傅臘塔馬如龍

translations.literal: Ge Ergu'e, Jin Shide, Zhao Shilin, Guo Shilong, Fu Lata, Ma Rulong
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ergu'e, Jin Shide, Zhao Shilin, Guo Shilong, Fu Lata, and Ma Rulong

sentences.zh: 格爾古德，字宜亭，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Ge Ergu'e, style name Yiting, of the Niohuru clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ergu'e, whose style was Yiting, belonged to the Niohuru clan and came from the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式授內院副理事官。

translations.literal: From the post of bithesi he was appointed associate director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the rank of bithesi clerk to become associate director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，從定西將軍圖海平湖廣茅麓山李自成餘部。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he followed the Pacifier of the West, General Tu Hai, in pacifying the remnant forces of Li Zicheng at Maolu Mountain in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 (1664) he followed General Tu Hai, the Pacifier of the West, in suppressing Li Zicheng's remaining followers at Maolu Mountain in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷弘文院侍讀，進翰林院侍讀學士，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was transferred to reader in the Hongwen Academy, advanced to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy, and served as daily lecturer and recorder of the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made a reader in the Hongwen Academy, then promoted to Hanlin reader-in-waiting and appointed daily lecturer and recorder of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從安親王岳樂討吳三桂。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed Prince An Yuele in campaigning against Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 (1674) he accompanied Prince An, Yuele, on the campaign against Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 三桂將林興珠降，上策請分水師，泊君山，斷常德道；

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui's general Lin Xingzhu surrendered, he submitted a plan asking that the fleet be divided, with ships anchored at Junshan to cut the Changde route;
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui's general Lin Xingzhu defected, Ge submitted a plan to split the fleet: station ships at Junshan to sever the Changde line;

sentences.zh: 泊香爐夾扁山，斷長沙、衡州道：則三桂將坐困。

translations.literal: and at Xianglu, Jiabian, and Bianshan to cut the Changsha and Hengzhou routes—then Wu Sangui's generals would be trapped in place.
translations.idiomatic: anchor others at Xianglu, Jiabian, and Bianshan to block the roads to Changsha and Hengzhou—so that Wu's commanders would be hemmed in.

sentences.zh: 安親王令格爾古德馳奏，並以興珠語聞，上密諭駐岳州諸將議行。

translations.literal: Prince An ordered Ge Ergu'e to ride posthaste with a memorial and also report Lin Xingzhu's words; the emperor secretly instructed the generals stationed at Yuezhou to deliberate and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Prince An had Ge Ergu'e rush a memorial to court and report Lin's proposal; the emperor secretly ordered the generals at Yuezhou to discuss and implement it.

sentences.zh: 師還，擢詹事，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent and transferred to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the army came home he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent and then made a grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授直隸巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed governor of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 (1682) he was appointed governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「金世德、於成龍為巡撫有聲，爾承其後，得名甚難。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him, saying: "Jin Shide and Yu Chenglong won renown as governors; you follow in their wake, and it will be very hard to win a name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "Jin Shide and Yu Chenglong were famous as governors. You follow in their footsteps, and earning a reputation will be difficult.

sentences.zh: 若急於求名，或致僨事，爾其懍諸！

translations.literal: If you are eager to seek a name, you may bring affairs to ruin—be on your guard!
translations.idiomatic: If you chase fame too eagerly you may ruin the work—take heed!

sentences.zh: 直隸旗下莊頭與民雜處，倚恃聲勢，每為民害。

translations.literal: In Zhili, estate managers under the banners live mixed among the people and, relying on their power, often harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhili, banner estate managers live among commoners and, leaning on their influence, often prey on the people.

sentences.zh: 爾其嚴察懲創，即皇莊亦毋寬宥。」

translations.literal: You must investigate strictly and punish; even imperial estates are not to be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: Investigate rigorously and punish offenders—even on the emperor's own estates, show no leniency."

sentences.zh: 八旗圈地屬於王公大臣者，輒置莊，設莊頭，主徵租，遂以病民，上深知之，故以諭格爾古德。

translations.literal: For allotted lands of the Eight Banners belonging to princes and great ministers, estates were always set up with managers to collect rent, and thus the people were afflicted; the emperor knew this well and therefore gave these instructions to Ge Ergu'e.
translations.idiomatic: On banner lands allotted to princes and high officials, estates were routinely established with rent-collecting managers who burdened the people—an abuse the emperor knew well, which is why he gave Ge Ergu'e these orders.

sentences.zh: 格爾古德尋疏言：「自鬻投旗之人，或作姦犯科，冀逃法網；

translations.literal: Ge Ergu'e soon memorialized, saying: "Those who sell themselves into the banners, some commit crimes hoping to escape the law;
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ergu'e soon memorialized: "People who sell themselves into banner households either commit crimes hoping to evade the law;

sentences.zh: 或遊手好閒，規避差徭。

translations.literal: or are idle and seek to evade corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: or are idlers who dodge corvée and tax duties.

sentences.zh: 本主聽其仍居本籍，放債牟利，則諱旗而稱民；

translations.literal: Their masters allow them to remain in their native places and lend money for profit; then they hide their banner status and call themselves commoners;
translations.idiomatic: Their masters let them stay in their home districts to lend at interest, and they hide their banner ties and pass as civilians;

sentences.zh: 窩逃構訟，遇官長訪聞，又舍民而稱旗。

translations.literal: they harbor fugitives and stir up lawsuits; when officials inquire, they again abandon the commoner label and claim banner status.
translations.idiomatic: they harbor fugitives and stir lawsuits; when officials investigate, they drop the civilian pretense and claim banner privilege.

sentences.zh: 詐害良善，官不敢問。

translations.literal: They swindle and harm the upright, and officials dare not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: They cheat honest people, and magistrates dare not touch them.

sentences.zh: 應責成本主，止留農戶在莊，餘俱收回服役。

translations.literal: The original master should be held responsible; only farming households should remain on the estate, and the rest should all be recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the original master accountable; keep only farming families on the estate and recall the rest to banner service.

sentences.zh: 有徇縱者議處。」

translations.literal: Whoever shows favoritism should be dealt with by deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who shields them should face disciplinary action."

sentences.zh: 下所司飭禁，並諭戶部：「凡鬻身之人，先經犯罪，投旗冀倖免者，與知情之本主，並從重治罪。」

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the relevant offices with orders to forbid it, and the Board of Revenue was instructed: "For all who sell their persons, if they had committed crimes beforehand and entered the banners hoping to escape punishment, together with the knowing original master, all are to be punished severely."
translations.idiomatic: The order went to the relevant offices, and the Board of Revenue was told: "Anyone who had committed a crime before selling himself into a banner to escape justice, together with a master who knew it, shall be punished severely."

sentences.zh: 時大學士明珠所屬佐領下人戶指圈民間塚地，民訴於戶部，事下巡撫，令宛平縣察勘。

translations.literal: At that time, households under the assistant banner commander subordinate to Grand Secretary Mingzhu claimed and enclosed commoners' grave lands; the people appealed to the Board of Revenue, the matter was sent to the governor, and Wanping county was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: About then, dependents of Assistant Banner Commander under Grand Secretary Mingzhu seized commoners' graveyards. The people appealed to the Board of Revenue; the case went to the governor, who ordered Wanping county to survey the site.

sentences.zh: 知縣王養濂言無礙民塚，格爾古德疏劾圈佔塚地屬實，養濂罣吏議。

translations.literal: Magistrate Wang Yanglian said there was no harm to commoners' graves; Ge Ergu'e memorialized impeaching him, and the enclosure of grave lands was found true; Yanglian was subject to official deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Wang Yanglian reported no harm to common graves, but Ge Ergu'e impeached him and proved the seizure true; Wang was referred for disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 詔嗣後有如此者，嚴懲不貸。

translations.literal: An edict declared that hereafter such cases would be severely punished without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that hereafter such offenses would be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 自康熙初，鼇拜柄政，總督硃昌祚等以圈地獲罪，由是無敢訟言其失者。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Kangxi, when Oboi held power, Governor Zhu Changzuo and others were punished for land enclosure, and thereafter none dared to litigate and speak of its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Since early Kangxi, when Oboi dominated the government, Governor Zhu Changzuo and others had been punished for protesting land seizures, and afterward no one dared sue over banner encroachments.

sentences.zh: 至奸民竄入旗下，尋仇傾陷，狡桀莫能製。

translations.literal: When scoundrels slipped into the banners, seeking revenge and framing others, their craft and violence could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: When ruffians slipped under banner protection to settle scores and frame rivals, their cunning lawlessness went unchecked.

sentences.zh: 獨格爾古德承上指，執法嚴懲，時稱為「鐵面」。

translations.literal: Only Ge Ergu'e, following the emperor's intent, enforced the law with strict punishment and was at the time called "Iron Face."
translations.idiomatic: Only Ge Ergu'e, acting on the emperor's intent, enforced the law relentlessly and was known as "Iron Face."

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上幸五台山，格爾古德迎駕，詢地方賢吏，以靈壽知縣陸隴其對。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the emperor visited Mount Wutai; Ge Ergu'e met the imperial progress and, when asked about worthy local officials, named Lingshou magistrate Lu Longqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 (1684), when the emperor visited Mount Wutai, Ge Ergu'e met the procession and, asked about capable local officials, named Lingshou magistrate Lu Longqi.

sentences.zh: 尋疏薦井陘道李基和、盧龍知縣衛立鼎與隴其廉能，下部擢用。

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized recommending Jingxing circuit intendant Li Jihe, Lulong magistrate Wei Liding, and Longqi for integrity and ability; the ministries were ordered to promote them.
translations.idiomatic: He soon recommended Jingxing circuit intendant Li Jihe, Lulong magistrate Wei Liding, and Longqi for integrity and ability, and the court promoted them.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以疾乞休，優詔慰留。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, on grounds of illness he begged to retire; a gracious edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to retire on account of illness; the emperor graciously urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 會詔廷臣公舉清廉官，首以格爾古德列奏。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered court ministers jointly to recommend incorrupt officials, Ge Ergu'e was listed first in the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was ordered to nominate incorrupt officials, Ge Ergu'e headed the list.

sentences.zh: 上念其羸疾，遣御醫診視。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of his frail illness, sent an imperial physician to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his frail health, the emperor sent an imperial physician to treat him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，賜卹加等，諡文清。

translations.literal: Before long he died; funeral favors were granted at an elevated grade, and he was given the posthumous title Wengqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; the court granted enhanced funeral honors and the posthumous title Wengqing (Cultured and Pure).

sentences.zh: 格爾古德清介，布衣蔬食，卻餽遺，纖毫不以自污。

translations.literal: Ge Ergu'e was pure and upright: coarse cloth and plain food, refusing gifts—he would not stain himself with the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ergu'e was incorruptible—he wore plain clothes, ate simple food, refused gifts, and would not let the smallest bribe touch him.

sentences.zh: 上嘗責漕運總督碩幹居官無狀，碩幹言：「臣為眾所忌，故未能致聲譽。」

translations.literal: The emperor once rebuked Grain Transport Director-general Shuogan for misconduct in office; Shuogan said, "Your servant is envied by many, and therefore has been unable to win a reputation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once rebuked Grain Transport Director-general Shuogan for poor conduct in office. Shuogan replied, "Your servant is widely envied, and so I have failed to win a good name."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「格爾古德為巡撫，沒後人猶思慕稱頌。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When Ge Ergu'e was governor, after his death people still remembered him with longing and praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Ge Ergu'e was governor, people still mourned and praised him after his death.

sentences.zh: 居官苟善，豈有不致聲譽者？」

translations.literal: If one serves in office with genuine goodness, how could one fail to win a reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: If you truly govern well, how can you fail to earn a reputation?"

sentences.zh: 為上所重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he valued by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the emperor held him.

sentences.zh: 祀直隸名宦。

translations.literal: He was enshrined among the famous officials of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was entered in the shrine of eminent officials of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 金世德，字孟求，漢軍正黃旗人，兵部侍郎維城子。

translations.literal: Jin Shide, style name Mengqiu, was a man of the Chinese Bordered Yellow Banner and son of Vice Minister of War Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shide, whose style was Mengqiu, came from the Chinese Bordered Yellow Banner and was the son of Vice Minister of War Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 淹貫經史，精國書。

translations.literal: He was steeped in the classics and histories and excelled in the national script.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply versed in the classics and histories and skilled in Manchu script.

sentences.zh: 以廕生授內院博士，累擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed doctor of the Inner Court and was repeatedly promoted to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he became a doctor of the Inner Court and rose to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授直隸巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 (1668) he was appointed governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 是時尚循明製，直隸不置兩司，世德請設守道理錢穀，巡道理刑名，如外省布政、按察二司。

translations.literal: At that time the Ming system was still followed and Zhili had no dual commissioners; Shide requested that circuit intendants handle revenue and grain, and circuit judges handle criminal cases, like the provincial administration and surveillance commissions elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili still followed the Ming pattern without provincial commissioners; Shide asked that circuit intendants handle fiscal affairs and circuit judges handle criminal cases, as in other provinces.

sentences.zh: 由是始有專司。

translations.literal: From this there began to be dedicated offices.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated offices were established as a result.

sentences.zh: 畿北諸郡，旗、民雜處，易於容姦，請立屯長以治之。

translations.literal: In the northern capital districts, banners and commoners lived mixed together, easily harboring wrongdoing; he requested village heads be established to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: In the districts north of the capital, where banners and commoners lived side by side and crime was easy to hide, he asked that village heads be appointed to keep order.

sentences.zh: 唐縣等三十七州縣，田一千六百餘頃，河流沙擁，民不能耕。

translations.literal: In thirty-seven prefectures and counties including Tang county, more than 1,600 qing of fields were choked by river sand and the people could not farm.
translations.idiomatic: In thirty-seven prefectures and counties including Tang, more than 1,600 qing of farmland were buried under river sand and could not be cultivated.

sentences.zh: 歲輸銀二萬有奇、穀豆三百九十石，歷年責原戶納賦為民害，世德為奏請除額。

translations.literal: Each year more than twenty thousand taels of silver and three hundred ninety shi of grain and beans were due; year after year the original households were compelled to pay tax, harming the people; Shide memorialized requesting removal of the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tax rolls still demanded more than twenty thousand taels of silver and three hundred ninety shi of grain yearly from the original households—a burden Shide had removed by memorial.

sentences.zh: 地震通州等九州縣，復請賑恤，並蠲免錢糧。

translations.literal: When earthquakes struck nine prefectures and counties including Tongzhou, he again requested relief and exemption of taxes and grain levies.
translations.idiomatic: After earthquakes struck nine prefectures and counties including Tongzhou, he again sought relief and tax exemptions.

sentences.zh: 皆如所請行。

translations.literal: All were carried out as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved every request.

sentences.zh: 師南征，供億繁急。

translations.literal: When the army marched south, supplies were urgently heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern campaign began, supply demands grew urgent.

sentences.zh: 世德單騎行營中，躬料芻糗，軍無橫索，吏無侵漁，市肆晏然。

translations.literal: Shide rode alone through the camps, personally overseeing fodder and rations; the army made no arbitrary demands, clerks did not extort, and markets were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Shide rode alone through the camps to oversee fodder and rations himself; troops did not requisition at will, clerks did not extort, and markets stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒，諡清惠。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; he was given the posthumous title Qinghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 19 (1680) and was posthumously titled Qinghui (Pure and Kind).

sentences.zh: 趙士麟，字麟伯，雲南河陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shilin, style name Linbo, was a native of Heyang in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shilin, whose style was Linbo, came from Heyang in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年進士，授貴州平遠推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Kangxi, he was appointed investigating censor of Pingyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination in Kangxi 3 (1664), he was appointed investigating censor of Pingyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 改直隸容城知縣，緝盜衛民，創正學書院，與諸生講學。

translations.literal: Transferred to be magistrate of Rongcheng in Zhili, he suppressed bandits to protect the people, founded the Zhengxue Academy, and lectured students.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Rongcheng in Zhili as magistrate, he suppressed bandits, founded the Zhengxue Academy, and lectured students.

sentences.zh: 行取，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: Selected by special promotion, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for capital service, he was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，擢光祿寺少卿，三遷至左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served as a bureau director, was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and after three transfers reached left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through bureau director posts to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and, after three promotions, to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏請台灣改郡縣比內地，設總兵鎮守，省沿海之戍卒，詔報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that Taiwan be made into prefectures and counties like the interior, with a regional commander stationed to guard it and coastal garrison troops reduced; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reorganize Taiwan into prefectures and counties like the interior, garrison it with a regional commander, and reduce coastal troops; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 (1684) he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 杭州民貸於駐防旗兵，名為「印子錢」，取息重，至鬻妻孥賣田舍；

translations.literal: Hangzhou commoners borrowed from garrison banner soldiers in loans called "seal-money," with heavy interest, until they sold wives and children and disposed of houses and fields;
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou commoners borrowed from garrison banner troops in loans called "seal-money" at crushing interest, until they sold wives, children, and farms;

sentences.zh: 不償，則閧於官。

translations.literal: if they did not repay, they would mob the magistrate's office.
translations.idiomatic: and when they could not repay, they mobbed the yamen.

sentences.zh: 營兵馬化龍毆官，成大獄。

translations.literal: Garrison soldier Ma Hualong beat an official, and the affair became a major case.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison soldier Ma Hualong assaulted an official, the affair blew into a major case.

sentences.zh: 士麟移會將軍掣繳券約，捐資代償。

translations.literal: Shilin sent a communication to the general to seize and cancel the loan contracts and contributed funds to repay on the people's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin wrote the garrison general to seize and cancel the loan contracts and contributed funds to pay the debts for the people.

sentences.zh: 將軍令減子歸母，母复減十之六。

translations.literal: The general ordered interest reduced to principal; Shilin further reduced it by six-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The general ordered interest cut to principal only; Shilin further reduced the burden by sixty percent.

sentences.zh: 事遂解，民大稱頌。

translations.literal: The matter was thus settled, and the people greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis ended, and the people praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 詔裁浙江總督，總督駐衢州，督標兵三千被汰，乏食譁掠，民罷市。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the post of Zhejiang governor-general; the governor-general was stationed at Quzhou, and three thousand troops of his command were cut; short of food they rioted and plundered, and the people closed their markets.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhejiang governor-generalship was abolished, the former governor-general at Quzhou lost three thousand troops to cuts; starving, they rioted and looted, and towns shut their markets.

sentences.zh: 士麟仍濟以餉，因奏設副將一，定額兵八百餘，留撥各營缺額。

translations.literal: Shilin still supplied them with rations and memorialized to establish one deputy commander with a fixed quota of more than eight hundred troops, retaining allocations from vacancies in the various camps.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin still fed them from provincial funds and memorialized to create a deputy commander post with eight hundred regular troops, drawing on vacant quotas from other camps.

sentences.zh: 眾乃定。

translations.literal: The masses were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Order was restored.

sentences.zh: 浙中豪右衙蠹，驕悍不法，為民害。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang powerful families and yamen parasites were arrogant, violent, and lawless, harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful clans and yamen parasites in Zhejiang were arrogant and lawless, preying on the people.

sentences.zh: 士麟廉得其狀，悉置之法，強暴斂跡。

translations.literal: Shilin investigated and learned the facts, punished all according to law, and the violent withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin investigated thoroughly, punished them all by law, and the bullies fell silent.

sentences.zh: 省城河道久淤，督役疏濬，半載訖工，民以為便。

translations.literal: The provincial capital's waterways had long been silted; he supervised labor to dredge them, and in half a year the work was finished, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's canals had long been choked with silt; he supervised dredging that finished in half a year to public relief.

sentences.zh: 复繕城隍，修學校，親蒞書院，與諸生講論經史及濂、洛、關、閩之學，士風大振。

translations.literal: He also repaired the city walls and moat, restored schools, personally attended the academy, and with students discussed the classics and histories and the learning of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min; scholarly morale was greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the walls and moat, restored schools, lectured at the academy on the classics and the Song Neo-Confucian traditions of Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and the Fujian school, and scholarly morale revived sharply.

sentences.zh: 禁革規費，積弊一清。

translations.literal: He forbade and abolished customary fees, and long-standing abuses were cleared at once.
translations.idiomatic: He banned illicit customary fees and swept away entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，移撫江蘇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to govern Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 (1686) he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 浙人懷之，繪圖以志去思，並於西湖敬一書院肖像祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Zhejiang cherished him, painted pictures to record their longing at his departure, and at West Lake in the Jingyi Academy enshrined his portrait in worship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang people missed him, commissioned paintings to remember his departure, and enshrined his portrait at the Jingyi Academy on West Lake.

sentences.zh: 尋召為兵部督捕侍郎，調吏部，皆能舉其職。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as vice minister of War in charge of pursuit and arrest, then transferred to Personnel; in each post he fulfilled his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice minister of War in charge of pursuit and arrest, then moved to Personnel; in each post he performed admirably.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 37 (1698).

sentences.zh: 祀浙江名宦。

translations.literal: He was enshrined among the famous officials of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was entered in the shrine of eminent officials of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 士麟潛心正學，以硃子為歸。

translations.literal: Shilin devoted himself to orthodox learning and took Master Zhu as his guide.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin devoted himself to orthodox learning with Zhu Xi as his guide.

sentences.zh: 躬行實踐，施於政事，士愨民恬，所至皆有聲績。

translations.literal: He practiced it in person and applied it in government; scholars were honest and the people at ease; wherever he went he left a renowned record.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced what he taught in government; scholars grew upright and the people content; wherever he served he left a celebrated record.

sentences.zh: 郭世隆，字昌伯，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Guo Shilong, style name Changbo, was a man of the Chinese Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shilong, whose style was Changbo, came from the Chinese Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 父洪臣，原籍汾州。

translations.literal: His father Hongchen was originally from Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongchen was a native of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，英親王阿濟格下九江，洪臣隨明將左夢庚來降，入旗，授佐領，分轄降眾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Prince Ying Ajige descended on Jiujiang; Hongchen followed the Ming general Zuo Menggeng in surrender, entered the banners, was appointed assistant banner commander, and administered the surrendered masses.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 (1645), when Prince Ying Ajige took Jiujiang, Hongchen followed the Ming general Zuo Menggeng in surrender, entered the banners as an assistant banner commander, and governed the surrendered troops.

sentences.zh: 累官湖廣道州總兵。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to regional commander of Daozhou in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became regional commander of Daozhou in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，世隆襲管佐領，授禮部員外郎，改御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, Shilong inherited management of the assistant banner command, was appointed a department vice director in the Ministry of Rites, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 (1665) Shilong inherited his father's assistant banner command, became a vice director in the Ministry of Rites, and was transferred to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，盛京福陵守兵訴其兄冤死，命世隆往按，得誣良刑偪自縊狀，原審侍郎阿禮瑚等坐失實奪官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, guards of the Fuling mausoleum in Mukden appealed that his elder brother had died unjustly; Shilong was ordered to investigate and found a case of framing the innocent, torture, and forced suicide; the original reviewing vice minister Alihu and others were punished for false findings and lost their posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 (1688), guards at Mukden's Fuling mausoleum appealed that Shilong's brother had been wrongfully killed; ordered to investigate, he proved framing, torture, and forced suicide, and the original reviewers, including Vice Minister Alihu, were stripped of office for false findings.

sentences.zh: 頃之，超擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted by exception to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 聖祖謁孝陵，經通州，山西禮縣民訴知縣萬世緯及知府紀元婪索狀，命世隆會督撫按治。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor visited the Xiaoling mausoleum and passed through Tongzhou, people of Lixian in Shanxi appealed against magistrate Wan Shiwei and prefect Ji Yuan for extortion; Shilong was ordered to join the governor-general and governor in investigating.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor visited the Xiaoling mausoleum and passed Tongzhou, people of Lixian in Shanxi accused Magistrate Wan Shiwei and Prefect Ji Yuan of extortion; Shilong was ordered to investigate jointly with the governor-general and governor.

sentences.zh: 世緯坐貪婪、科派、杖斃無罪人，元坐受賕薦世緯卓異，皆論死。

translations.literal: Shiwei was convicted of greed, illegal levies, and beating to death persons without crime; Yuan was convicted of taking bribes and recommending Shiwei as outstanding; all were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwei was sentenced to death for greed, illegal levies, and beating innocents to death; Yuan was sentenced to death for taking bribes and falsely recommending Shiwei as outstanding.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，代於成龍為直隸巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he replaced Yu Chenglong as governor of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 (1690) he succeeded Yu Chenglong as governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 先是，罷任安溪知縣孫鏞告福建巡撫張仲舉、布政使張永茂侵蝕庫帑，遣郎中吳爾泰會總督勘訊，至即拘訊知府六人，連引州縣官數十人。

translations.literal: Earlier, dismissed Anxi magistrate Sun Yong had accused Fujian governor Zhang Zhongju and provincial administration commissioner Zhang Yongmao of embezzling the treasury; Bureau Director Wu Ertai was sent with the governor-general to investigate; on arrival he at once detained and interrogated six prefects and implicated dozens of prefectural and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, dismissed Anxi magistrate Sun Yong had accused Fujian Governor Zhang Zhongju and Administration Commissioner Zhang Yongmao of embezzling provincial funds; Bureau Director Wu Ertai was sent with the governor-general to investigate, and on arrival immediately detained six prefects and implicated dozens of county and prefectural officials.

sentences.zh: 上聞疑之，命世隆往按，發仲舉與前布政使張汧竄改賦冊、侵隱已徵額銀捏作民欠，又汧遷湖廣巡撫虧福建庫帑三十餘萬，仲舉前任湖南布政亦虧帑，相約互抵；

translations.literal: The emperor heard and doubted; Shilong was ordered to investigate and uncovered that Zhongju and former administration commissioner Zhang Qian had tampered with tax registers, concealed collected quota silver and fabricated popular arrears; moreover Qian, transferred to Huguang as governor, had left a Fujian treasury shortfall of more than three hundred thousand; Zhongju, formerly Hunan administration commissioner, had also had a treasury shortfall—they had agreed to offset each other;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and sent Shilong to investigate. He found that Zhongju and former Administration Commissioner Zhang Qian had altered tax registers, concealed collected revenues, and fabricated popular arrears; Zhang Qian, now Huguang governor, had left Fujian's treasury short more than three hundred thousand taels, and Zhongju had done the same in Hunan—they had agreed to cover for each other;

sentences.zh: 嗣仲舉聞汧以贓敗，而福建庫尚未完，飭屬代為彌縫，左證悉合。

translations.literal: later, when Zhongju heard Qian had fallen on corruption charges while the Fujian treasury was still incomplete, he ordered subordinates to cover the gap—all corroborating evidence matched.
translations.idiomatic: and when Zhang Qian fell on corruption charges while Fujian's books were still short, Zhongju ordered subordinates to paper over the gap—all evidence aligned.

sentences.zh: 仲舉、永茂俱論罪如律。

translations.literal: Zhongju and Yongmao were both punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju and Yongmao were both sentenced under the law.

sentences.zh: 世隆之任，帝諭曰：「於成龍居官甚善，繼之不易，爾當勤慎任事。」

translations.literal: When Shilong took office, the emperor instructed him, saying: "Yu Chenglong served very well in office; succeeding him is not easy—you must be diligent and cautious in your duties."
translations.idiomatic: When Shilong took office, the emperor told him: "Yu Chenglong governed exceedingly well; succeeding him will not be easy—you must serve diligently and carefully."

sentences.zh: 順天、保定、真定、永平諸府旱，世隆奉命履勘，疏言：「被災者七十四州縣，請蠲本年及來年額賦。

translations.literal: In Shuntian, Baoding, Zhending, Yongping, and other prefectures there was drought; Shilong was ordered to inspect on foot and memorialized: "Seventy-four prefectures and counties suffered disaster; I request exemption of this year's and next year's quota taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Drought struck Shuntian, Baoding, Zhending, Yongping, and other prefectures; ordered to inspect in person, Shilong memorialized that seventy-four prefectures and counties had been hit and asked to remit this year's and next year's tax quotas.

sentences.zh: 霸、文安等十四州縣災尤重，請治賑。」

translations.literal: In fourteen prefectures and counties including Ba and Wen'an the disaster was especially severe; I request organized relief."
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen prefectures and counties including Ba and Wen'an were hardest hit; he asked for organized relief."

sentences.zh: 迭疏籌積貯，並以奉天歲豐，請飭山海關暫聽民間轉糶，仍限肩挑馱負，不得以大車裝載，皆如所請。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to plan grain reserves, and because Fengtian had a bountiful year, requested that Shanhaiguan temporarily allow private grain transport, still limiting loads to shoulder poles and pack animals and forbidding large carts—all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly planned grain reserves and, because Fengtian had had a good harvest, asked that Shanhaiguan temporarily allow private grain shipments by pole and pack animal only, not by cart—all approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「真定地當衝要，所屬贊皇縣，西有大峪曰子午套，素為盜藪，請移紫荊關副將駐真定；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Zhending lies on a vital route; its Zanhuang county to the west has a great ravine called Ziwutao, long a bandit lair; I request the deputy commander of Zijing Pass be moved to station at Zhending;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that Zhending lay on a vital route and that Zanhuang county to the west had a bandit haunt called Ziwutao; he asked that the Zijing Pass deputy commander be stationed at Zhending;

sentences.zh: 調馬、步兵二千分防霸州。」

translations.literal: and two thousand cavalry and infantry be transferred to garrison Bazhou in detachments."
translations.idiomatic: and that two thousand cavalry and infantry be redeployed to garrison Bazhou."

sentences.zh: 子牙河決，淹沒田畝，請修築大城等縣堤岸，並濬王家口、黑龍港諸支流堙塞者，皆報可。

translations.literal: When the Ziya River burst its banks and flooded fields, he requested dikes be built in Dacheng and other counties and tributaries such as Wangjiakou and Heilonggang be dredged where blocked—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ziya River burst and flooded farmland, he asked to rebuild dikes in Dacheng and other counties and dredge blocked tributaries such as Wangjiakou and Heilonggang—all approved.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 34 (1695) he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 歲歉，率閉糴居奇。

translations.literal: In years of scarcity, people generally hoarded grain and held it for monopoly prices.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years merchants hoarded grain to drive up prices.

sentences.zh: 世隆疏請蠲賦，並發帑二十萬，乞糴江、浙，海運平糶，詔俞之。

translations.literal: Shilong memorialized requesting tax remission and disbursement of two hundred thousand taels from the treasury to buy grain in Jiangsu and Zhejiang and sell it at fair prices by sea transport; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sought tax relief and two hundred thousand taels from the treasury to buy grain in Jiangsu and Zhejiang and sell it fairly by sea; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 先是浙省奏請鼓鑄，官吏射利，請減其分數。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhejiang had memorialized requesting minting; officials sought profit and requested the alloy proportion be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhejiang had sought permission to mint coin; officials profited by debasing the alloy.

sentences.zh: 由是私鑄者眾，每錢不及七八分，壅滯不行。

translations.literal: Hence private minting was widespread; each coin was less than seven or eight fen in value and clogged circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Private minting flourished; coins were worth less than seven or eight fen each and would not circulate.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，世隆迎駕，至杭州，民擁輿赴訴。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the emperor made a southern tour; Shilong met the imperial progress; at Hangzhou the people crowded his sedan chair to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 (1699), during the southern tour, Shilong met the emperor at Hangzhou, where people mobbed his chair with petitions.

sentences.zh: 乃停官爐，發帑收毀私錢，錢得流布。

translations.literal: He then halted the official mints, disbursed treasury funds to buy up and destroy private coin, and currency circulated again.
translations.idiomatic: He halted the official mints, used treasury funds to buy up and melt private coin, and currency circulated again.

sentences.zh: 上聞，為褒美。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him when he heard.

sentences.zh: 鄞縣沿海田，被水沖決一千七十餘畝，請永免額賦。

translations.literal: Coastal fields in Yin county, more than 1,070 mu washed away by water, he requested permanently exempt from quota tax.
translations.idiomatic: More than 1,070 mu of coastal fields in Yin county had been washed away; he asked for permanent tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，調兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was transferred to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 41 (1702) he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 廣東海疆二千餘裡，守汛遼闊，盜賊出沒無常。

translations.literal: Guangdong's maritime frontier was more than two thousand li; garrison posts were far apart and bandits appeared and vanished unpredictably.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong's coast stretched more than two thousand li; garrisons were thin and pirates came and went unpredictably.

sentences.zh: 世隆疏定營製，增設兵船巡哨，迭擊敗海盜，沉其舟四十五。

translations.literal: Shilong memorialized to fix camp regulations, add military ships for patrol, repeatedly defeated sea bandits, and sank forty-five of their vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong standardized camp organization, added patrol vessels, repeatedly defeated pirates, and sank forty-five of their ships.

sentences.zh: 疏報擒海陽巨盜蔡玉也等五人。

translations.literal: He memorialized reporting the capture of the great Haiyang bandit Cai Yuye and four others.
translations.idiomatic: He reported capturing the Haiyang bandit chief Cai Yuye and four accomplices.

sentences.zh: 上遣刑部侍郎常綬往勘，因議世隆平時禁賊不嚴，盜發，朦朧掩飾，坐奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Vice Minister of Punishments Chang Shou to investigate; it was concluded that in peaceful times Shilong had not strictly forbidden bandits, that piracy broke out, and that he had vaguely concealed it—he was punished by loss of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister of Punishments Chang Shou to investigate; Shilong was found to have been lax about piracy in peacetime and to have glossed over the outbreak, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，起湖廣總督、疏陳防守紅苗，請沿邊安設塘汛，禁內地民與苗往來，並勿與為婚姻。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was recalled as governor-general of Huguang; he memorialized on defending the Red Miao, requesting watch posts along the border, forbidding interior people to trade with the Miao, and also forbidding intermarriage.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 46 (1707) he was recalled as Huguang governor-general and memorialized on defending the Red Miao, asking for border watch posts, a ban on trade between interior people and the Miao, and a ban on intermarriage.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五十年，以山西流匪陳四等潛入湖廣，鳩黨劫掠，世隆前任總督坐失察，奪官。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, because Shanxi roaming bandits Chen Si and others had slipped into Huguang, gathered followers, and plundered, Shilong as former governor-general was punished for failure to detect and lost his post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 50 (1711), when Shanxi bandits led by Chen Si infiltrated Huguang and raided, Shilong was punished for failing to detect them during his earlier term and lost his post.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，萬壽，復原品。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, at the imperial birthday celebration, his original rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 (1713), at the imperial birthday celebration, his original rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 居三年，卒。

translations.literal: After three years in office he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 直隸、福建、浙江、兩廣、湖廣皆祀名宦。

translations.literal: He was enshrined among famous officials in Zhili, Fujian, Zhejiang, the Two Guangs, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was entered in the shrines of eminent officials in Zhili, Fujian, Zhejiang, the Two Guangs, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 傅臘塔，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Fu Lata, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lata, of the Irgen Gioro clan, came from the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式授內閣中書，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: From bithesi he was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat and transferred to reader.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from bithesi clerk to Grand Secretariat secretary and then reader.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，授山東道御史，有聲台中。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi he was appointed censor of the Shandong circuit and gained renown in the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 (1680) he became censor of the Shandong circuit and won renown at court.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，出為陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he went out as administration commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 (1686) he became administration commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢左副都御史，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief and transferred to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 (1687) he was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief and made vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，偕侍郎多奇往雲南按提督萬正色與總兵王珍互訐事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, together with Vice Minister Duoqi, he went to Yunnan to investigate the mutual accusations between Regional Commander Wan Zhengse and Regional Commander Wang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 (1688) he went with Vice Minister Duoqi to Yunnan to investigate mutual accusations between Regional Commander Wan Zhengse and Regional Commander Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 讞實，正色、珍俱論罪有差。

translations.literal: The case was verified; Zhengse and Zhen were both punished with differing sentences.
translations.idiomatic: The charges were proved; both were punished, though not equally.

sentences.zh: 調吏部，授兩江總督。

translations.literal: Transferred to Personnel, he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Personnel, he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上諭曰：「爾當潔己奉公，督兩江無如於成龍者，爾效之可矣！」

translations.literal: At his audience of leave, the emperor instructed: "You must keep yourself pure and serve the public; among governors of the Two Jiangs none equals Yu Chenglong—you may emulate him!"
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said: "Keep yourself pure and serve the public. Among Two Jiangs governors none equals Yu Chenglong—follow his example!"

sentences.zh: 傅臘塔至官，清弊政，斥貪墨，讞獄尤明慎。

translations.literal: When Fu Lata reached his post he cleared abusive policies, expelled the corrupt, and was especially clear and cautious in deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: At his post Fu Lata swept away abuses, expelled the corrupt, and judged cases with exceptional clarity and care.

sentences.zh: 贛縣民訴知縣劉瀚芳私徵銀米十餘萬，並蠹役不法。

translations.literal: People of Gan county appealed that Magistrate Liu Hanfang had privately levied more than one hundred thousand taels of silver and grain, and that corrupt clerks acted unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: People of Gan county accused Magistrate Liu Hanfang of privately levying more than one hundred thousand taels of silver and grain and of corrupt clerks acting unlawfully.

sentences.zh: 傅臘塔因劾布政使多弘安、按察使吳延貴、贛南道鍾有德於吏役婪贓不速勘，復從輕擬，曲為庇護，弘安、延貴、有德並坐罷。

translations.literal: Fu Lata therefore impeached Administration Commissioner Duo Hong'an, Surveillance Commissioner Wu Yangui, and Gannan circuit intendant Zhong Youde for not promptly investigating clerks' greedy corruption, then recommending lenient sentences and bending the law to shield them—Hong'an, Yangui, and Youde were all punished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lata impeached Administration Commissioner Duo Hong'an, Surveillance Commissioner Wu Yangui, and Gannan Circuit Intendant Zhong Youde for delaying investigation of corrupt clerks, recommending lenient sentences, and shielding the guilty—all three were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上南巡，閱運河，命傅臘塔會河道總督王新命勘儀真河閘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor toured south, inspected the Grand Canal, and ordered Fu Lata to join Canal Director-general Wang Xinming in surveying the Yizhen river sluice.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28 (1689), during the southern tour, the emperor inspected the Grand Canal and ordered Fu Lata and Canal Director-general Wang Xinming to survey the Yizhen sluice.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「閘外為北新洲，北新洲外又有漲沙平鋪江中。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Outside the sluice is Beixinzhou; beyond Beixinzhou rising sand lies flat across the river.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that beyond the sluice lay Beixinzhou, and beyond that rising sand lay flat across the river.

sentences.zh: 應疏北新洲支河，直通四閘。

translations.literal: The Beixinzhou branch should be dredged to connect directly with the four sluices.
translations.idiomatic: The Beixinzhou branch should be dredged to connect directly with the four sluices.

sentences.zh: 糧艘循漲沙尾入新河口，可以通行。」

translations.literal: Grain transports could follow the tail of the rising sand into the new river mouth and pass through."
translations.idiomatic: Grain transports could follow the edge of the sandbar into the new mouth and pass through."

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「江寧廛稅累民，內輸房稅，外輸廊鈔，更外輸棚租，請予蠲免。」

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said: "Jiangning market taxes burden the people: inner payment of house tax, outer payment of gallery fees, and beyond that shed rent—I request exemption."
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he said Jiangning's market taxes burdened the people with house tax, gallery fees, and shed rent, and asked that they be remitted."

sentences.zh: 皆如所請。

translations.literal: All were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，淮、徐飢，發常平倉穀賑恤，災民賴焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Huai and Xu suffered famine; he released grain from the ever-normal granaries for relief, and disaster victims relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 (1690), when Huai and Xu suffered famine, he released ever-normal granary grain for relief on which the victims depended.

sentences.zh: 蘆洲丈量，例委佐貳，民苦需索。

translations.literal: For Luzhou land surveys, deputy officials were routinely delegated, and the people suffered extortionate demands.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou land surveys were routinely delegated to deputies, and the people suffered extortion.

sentences.zh: 傅臘塔定五年一行，悉以印官理其事。

translations.literal: Fu Lata fixed a cycle of once every five years and had all matters handled by officials bearing the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lata ordered surveys once every five years and required sealed officials to conduct them.

sentences.zh: 歷年逋賦，量為帶徵，由是積困頓甦。

translations.literal: Arrears accumulated over years were collected in measured installments, and thus long-standing distress revived.
translations.idiomatic: Years of tax arrears were collected in measured installments, and long-standing distress eased.

sentences.zh: 是年，監臨江南鄉試，疏稱士子應試者萬有餘人，請廣科舉額，下部議，增廣額四十名。

translations.literal: That year, supervising the Jiangnan provincial examination, he memorialized that more than ten thousand candidates had tested and requested expanded quotas; the ministries deliberated and added forty places.
translations.idiomatic: That year, supervising the Jiangnan provincial examination, he reported more than ten thousand candidates and asked for more places; the ministries added forty.

sentences.zh: 疏劾大學士徐元文、原任尚書徐乾學縱子弟招權罔利，巡撫洪之傑徇私袒庇。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Grand Secretary Xu Yuanwen and former minister Xu Qianxue for indulging their sons and younger relatives in seizing power for profit, and Governor Hong Zhijie for partiality and shielding them.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Grand Secretary Xu Yuanwen and former Minister Xu Qianxue for letting their sons seize power for profit, and Governor Hong Zhijie for shielding them.

sentences.zh: 詔毋深究，予元文休致。

translations.literal: An edict ordered no deep investigation and granted Yuanwen retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered no deep investigation and allowed Yuanwen to retire.

sentences.zh: 沭陽民周廷鑑叩閽訟降調侍郎胡簡敬居鄉不法，並及之傑瞻徇狀，命傅臘塔按治，得實，簡敬及其子弟並治罪，之傑奪官。

translations.literal: A Shuyang commoner, Zhou Tingjian, knocked at the palace gate to sue the demoted Vice Minister Hu Jianjing for lawless conduct in his home district, also implicating Hong Zhijie's favoritism; Fu Lata was ordered to investigate, found the facts true, punished Jianjing and his sons and younger relatives, and stripped Zhijie of office.
translations.idiomatic: A Shuyang man, Zhou Tingjian, petitioned at the palace gate against demoted Vice Minister Hu Jianjing for misconduct at home and Governor Hong Zhijie's favoritism; Fu Lata investigated, proved the charges, punished Hu and his sons, and stripped Hong of office.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，廣東巡撫江有良與巡鹽太常少卿沙拜互訐。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Guangdong Governor Jiang Youliang and Salt Inspector, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Shabei, mutually accused each other.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 32 (1693), Guangdong Governor Jiang Youliang and Salt Inspector Shabei mutually accused each other.

sentences.zh: 傅臘塔往按，有良、沙拜並坐受賕，奪官。

translations.literal: Fu Lata went to investigate; Youliang and Shabei were both convicted of taking bribes and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lata investigated; both were convicted of bribery and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，疏言：「淮、揚所屬多版荒，巡撫宋犖曾請緩徵，格於部議。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he memorialized: "Under Huai and Yang many fields are registered as waste; Governor Song Luo once requested deferred collection, but the ministries blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 33 (1694) he memorialized that many fields under Huai and Yang were registered as waste land; Governor Song Luo's request for deferred collection had been blocked by the ministries.

sentences.zh: 臣履畝詳勘，鹽城、高郵等州縣因遇水災，業戶逃亡者眾。

translations.literal: Your servant has walked the fields and surveyed in detail: in Yancheng, Gaoyou, and other prefectures and counties, because of flood many landowners have fled.
translations.idiomatic: Walking the fields himself, he found that in Yancheng, Gaoyou, and other districts floods had driven away many landowners.

sentences.zh: 今田有涸出之名，人無耕種之實，小民積困。

translations.literal: Now the fields have the name of land emerged from water, but in reality no one cultivates; the common people are deeply distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were listed as reclaimed from flood but in fact lay uncultivated, and the people were crushed by debt.

sentences.zh: 熟田額糧尚多懸欠，何能代償盈萬之荒賦？

translations.literal: On cultivated land the quota grain still has much outstanding—how can they pay in place of tens of thousands in waste-land tax?
translations.idiomatic: Even cultivated land still owed heavy quotas—how could farmers also pay tens of thousands in tax on waste fields?

sentences.zh: 請恩賜蠲除，庶逃戶懷歸，安居樂業。」

translations.literal: I request gracious exemption so that fugitive households may wish to return and live and work in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for gracious remission so fugitives would return and settle in peace.

sentences.zh: 疏入，下部議，不許，上特命免徵。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the ministries deliberated and refused; the emperor specially ordered exemption.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries refused, but the emperor personally ordered exemption.

sentences.zh: 旋卒於官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office soon after.

sentences.zh: 上聞，諭廷臣曰：「傅臘塔和而不流，不畏權勢，愛惜軍民。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he instructed the court ministers: "Fu Lata was harmonious yet not unprincipled, feared no power, and cherished soldiers and people.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he told the court: "Fu Lata was conciliatory but principled, feared no power, and cared for soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督居官善者，於成龍而後，惟傅臘塔。」

translations.literal: Among governors of the Two Jiangs who served well, after Yu Chenglong there was only Fu Lata."
translations.idiomatic: Among Two Jiangs governors who served well, after Yu Chenglong there was only Fu Lata."

sentences.zh: 遣太僕寺卿楊舒赴江寧致祭，贈太子太保，諡清端，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Yang Shu to Jiangning to offer sacrifice, posthumously granted him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Qingduan, and a hereditary commandant of cavalry post.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister Yang Shu to Jiangning to offer sacrifice, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Qingduan (Pure and Upright), and granted a hereditary commandant of cavalry post.

sentences.zh: 士民懷之，為建祠江寧。

translations.literal: Scholars and people cherished him and built a shrine for him in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners cherished him and built a shrine in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，上南巡，經雨花台，賜祠額曰「兩江遺愛」。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, on a southern tour passing Yuhuatai, the emperor bestowed on the shrine the plaque "Two Jiangs' Enduring Grace."
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 44 (1705), on a southern tour past Yuhuatai, the emperor bestowed the plaque "Two Jiangs' Enduring Grace."

sentences.zh: 雍正中，入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he was entered in the Shrine of Worthy Officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng reign he was entered in the Shrine of Worthy Officials.

sentences.zh: 馬如龍，字見五，陝西綏德州人。

translations.literal: Ma Rulong, style name Jianwu, was a native of Suide prefecture in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rulong, whose style was Jianwu, came from Suide in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the eleventh year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Kangxi 11 (1672).

sentences.zh: 十四年，陝西提督王輔臣據寧羌叛，其黨硃龍寇綏德，陷之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Shaanxi Provincial Commander Wang Fuchen rebelled holding Ningqiang; his follower Zhu Long raided Suide and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 (1675), Shaanxi Provincial Commander Wang Fuchen rebelled from Ningqiang; his follower Zhu Long raided and captured Suide.

sentences.zh: 如龍糾鄉勇倚山立寨，寇至，屢擊卻之。

translations.literal: Rulong gathered local braves, built a stockade on the mountain, and whenever bandits came repeatedly drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Rulong rallied local militia, built a mountain stockade, and repeatedly repelled the raiders.

sentences.zh: 輔臣誘以偽劄，斬其使。

translations.literal: Fuchen tried to entice him with a forged dispatch; Rulong beheaded the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen tried to win him with a forged commission; Rulong beheaded the envoy.

sentences.zh: 會平逆將軍畢力克圖兵至，如龍渡河迎，呈偽劄，並陳賊虛實，因率所部為前鋒，克綏德。

translations.literal: When the Pacification General Biliketu arrived, Rulong crossed the river to meet him, presented the forged dispatch, and reported the rebels' strengths and weaknesses; he then led his force as vanguard and recovered Suide.
translations.idiomatic: When Pacification General Biliketu arrived, Rulong crossed the river to meet him, presented the forged dispatch, briefed him on rebel strength, led his men as vanguard, and recovered Suide.

sentences.zh: 畢力克圖以聞，即便宜令攝州事。

translations.literal: Biliketu reported it, and at once, by discretionary authority, ordered him to act as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Biliketu reported the feat and immediately authorized him to act as prefect.

sentences.zh: 總督哈佔亦疏言如龍倡義拒賊狀，請優敘。

translations.literal: Governor-general Hazhan also memorialized on Rulong's righteous resistance to the bandits and requested preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Hazhan also memorialized on Rulong's righteous resistance and asked for special recognition.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授直隸灤州知州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed prefect of Luanzhou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 (1677) he was appointed prefect of Luanzhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 州民猾而多盜，如龍鋤暴安良，豪右斂跡。

translations.literal: The prefecture's people were crafty and bandits numerous; Rulong uprooted violence and settled the good, and powerful families withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was rife with cunning people and bandits; Rulong suppressed violence and protected the law-abiding, and local bullies fell silent.

sentences.zh: 州有民殺人而埋其屍，四十年矣；

translations.literal: In the prefecture a man had killed someone and buried the body—forty years had passed;
translations.idiomatic: A murder had been buried in the prefecture forty years earlier;

sentences.zh: 如龍宿逆旅，得白骨，問之，曰：「此屋十易主矣。」

translations.literal: Rulong lodged at an inn, found white bones, and asked about them; he was told, "This house has changed owners ten times."
translations.idiomatic: lodging at an inn, Rulong found bones and was told, "This house has had ten owners."

sentences.zh: 縶最初一人至，鉤其情得實，置諸法。

translations.literal: He detained the very first owner, drew out the truth, and punished him by law.
translations.idiomatic: He detained the first owner, drew out a confession, and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 昌平有殺人獄不得其主名，使如龍按之。

translations.literal: In Changping there was a murder case without a named culprit; Rulong was sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When a Changping murder case had no named culprit, Rulong was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 閱狀，則民父子殺於僧寺，並及僧五，而民居旁二姓皆與民有連，問之，謝不知。

translations.literal: Reading the file, he found a father and son of a commoner household killed in a Buddhist temple, together with five monks; two surnames living beside the household were all connected with the family—questioned, they pleaded ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: The file showed a father and son killed in a temple along with five monks; two neighboring clans connected to the family denied all knowledge.

sentences.zh: 使蹟之，二人相與語曰：「孰謂馬公察，易欺耳。」

translations.literal: He had them tracked; the two said to each other, "Who says Prefect Ma is sharp—he's easy to fool."
translations.idiomatic: When he had them followed, the two said to each other, "Who says Prefect Ma is sharp? He's easy to fool."

sentences.zh: 執訊之，乃服。

translations.literal: Seized and interrogated, they then confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Seized and interrogated, they confessed.

sentences.zh: 自是民頌如龍能折獄。

translations.literal: From then on the people praised Rulong for his ability to decide cases.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the people praised Rulong for unraveling difficult cases.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以察出民間隱地，敘勞，入為戶部員外郎，歷刑部郎中，榷浙江北新關稅務。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, for uncovering concealed private land, his merit was recorded; he entered the capital as a department vice director in Revenue, served as a bureau director in Punishments, and supervised tax at Beixin Pass in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 (1680), rewarded for uncovering concealed land, he entered the capital as a Revenue vice director, became a Punishments bureau director, and supervised the Beixin Pass customs in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷杭州知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 (1685) he was made prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 杭州民貸於旗營，息重不能償，質及子女。

translations.literal: Hangzhou commoners borrowed from the banner garrison; interest was heavy and they could not repay, and pledges extended even to wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou commoners borrowed from the banner garrison at crushing interest they could not repay, pledging even wives and children.

sentences.zh: 如龍請於將軍，覈子母，以公使錢代償。

translations.literal: Rulong appealed to the general, verified principal and interest, and used public funds to repay on the people's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Rulong appealed to the garrison general, verified principal and interest, and used public funds to repay the debts.

sentences.zh: 杭州民咸頌如龍。

translations.literal: All Hangzhou people praised Rulong.
translations.idiomatic: All Hangzhou praised Rulong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上南巡，聞其治行，超擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, on the southern tour, the emperor heard of his conduct in office and promoted him by exception to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28 (1689), on the southern tour, the emperor heard of his record and promoted him to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 平反庶獄，多所全活。

translations.literal: He reversed wrongful cases and saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed wrongful convictions and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 海賊楊士玉竄跡島嶼，勾土賊胡茂等剽掠商船，如龍設策擒之，盡殲其首從，巡撫張鵬翮以聞。

translations.literal: Sea bandit Yang Shiyu hid on islands, colluded with local bandits Hu Mao and others to plunder merchant ships; Rulong devised a plan to capture them and wiped out leaders and followers; Governor Zhang Penghe reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandit Yang Shiyu hid on islands and, with local bandit Hu Mao and others, plundered merchant ships; Rulong captured them and wiped out the gang; Governor Zhang Penghe reported the feat.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷布政使，屬吏有歲餽，悉禁絕之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to administration commissioner; subordinates had yearly gifts—all were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 (1690) he became administration commissioner and forbade all yearly gifts from subordinates.

sentences.zh: 是年，紹興大水，庫儲絀，無可救濟。

translations.literal: That year Shaoxing suffered great flood; treasury stores were insufficient and there was nothing with which to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: That year a great flood struck Shaoxing; the treasury was empty and relief seemed impossible.

sentences.zh: 如龍檄十一郡合輸米二萬餘石，按戶賑給，告屬吏曰：「是逾於歲餽多矣，」

translations.literal: Rulong issued orders for eleven prefectures jointly to deliver more than twenty thousand shi of rice, distributed household by household for relief, and told subordinates, "This exceeds yearly gifts by far,"
translations.idiomatic: Rulong ordered eleven prefectures to deliver more than twenty thousand shi of rice for household relief and told his staff, "This is far more than your yearly gifts,"

sentences.zh: 三十一年，授江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31 (1692) he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 整飭常平倉，春以羨米出貸，秋收還倉。

translations.literal: He put the ever-normal granaries in order: in spring surplus grain was lent out, and at autumn harvest returned to the granary.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized the ever-normal granaries to lend surplus grain in spring and return it after harvest.

sentences.zh: 飭州縣廣積儲，備兇荒。

translations.literal: He ordered prefectures and counties to store grain widely in preparation for famine.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered prefectures and counties to build grain reserves against famine.

sentences.zh: 仿白鹿洞遺法，建書院以教士。

translations.literal: Following the legacy methods of White Deer Grotto, he built an academy to instruct scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Following the White Deer Grotto model, he founded an academy to educate scholars.

sentences.zh: 嚴溺女之禁。

translations.literal: He strictly enforced the prohibition on drowning infant girls.
translations.idiomatic: He strictly enforced the ban on female infanticide.

sentences.zh: 疏請罷追轉漕腳耗。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting an end to pursuing collection of grain-transport porterage surcharges.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to end the pursuit of grain-transport porterage surcharges.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，入覲，賜御書「老成清望」榜。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he came to audience and was granted an imperial inscription on a plaque reading "Mature Integrity and Clear Repute."
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 (1699) he attended court and received an imperial plaque inscribed "Mature Integrity and Clear Repute."

sentences.zh: 時淮、揚薦飢，如龍以江西連歲豐稔，率僚屬捐米十萬賑之。

translations.literal: At that time Huai and Yang suffered repeated famine; Rulong, because Jiangxi had had successive bountiful years, led his subordinates in donating one hundred thousand dan of rice for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai and Yang suffered repeated famine, Rulong, drawing on Jiangxi's successive good harvests, led his staff in donating one hundred thousand dan of rice for relief.

sentences.zh: 以老病累疏乞休，詔輒慰留。

translations.literal: On grounds of age and illness he repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; each time an edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Age and illness led him to beg repeatedly to retire; each time the emperor urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 四十年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he died; sacrificial funeral honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 40 (1701); the court granted sacrificial funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 論曰：守成世為大臣者，以仁心行仁政，培養元氣，其先務也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In an age of preserving the legacy, for great ministers the first task is to govern with a benevolent heart and benevolent policies and to nurture the vital energies of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: In an age of consolidation, great ministers must above all govern with benevolence and nurture the realm's vital energies.

sentences.zh: 兵革初息，瘡痍未復，格爾古德等任封疆之重，拊循安輯，與民休息，政績卓卓在耳目。

translations.literal: When arms had just ceased and wounds were not yet healed, Ge Ergu'e and others bore the heavy charge of frontier governance, soothed and settled the people, let them rest, and their achievements stood conspicuous before all eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When war had barely ended and the land still lay wounded, Ge Ergu'e and others bore heavy frontier responsibilities, soothed the people, let them recover, and left achievements plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 廷褒老成，野留遺愛，有以哉！

translations.literal: The court praised their mature integrity, and the countryside retained their enduring grace—how fitting!
translations.idiomatic: The court honored their mature integrity, and the people cherished their enduring grace—rightly so!
